title: Connexions de Gauss-Manin et équations de Picard-Fuchs. Opération de Cartier : copies de tapuscrit annoté (s.d.), tiré à part (1981), notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: this is part of a section on Dieudonné theory for abelian schemes, closely matching the text of Grothendieck's Nice 1970 ICM report 'Groupes de Barsotti-Tate et cristaux'. The previous page gives a first, cohomological construction of the Dieudonné crystal: D*(A)_{S'} = H^1_DR(A'/S'). It is filtered by the Hodge filtration 0 -> ω_A -> D*(A)_S -> t_{A*} -> 0. It also states the deformation theorem: abelian schemes over a nilpotent PD-thickening S' correspond to an abelian scheme A over S together with a locally direct-summand lift Fil^1 ⊂ D*(A)_{S'} of ω_A.

This page gives a second interpretation, meant to produce a quasi-inverse of the deformation functor. For an abelian scheme A/S take the universal vector extension 0 -> V(ω_{A*}) -> E(A) -> A -> 0. The vector group is the dual of the tangent space of A*, written with a check over t_{A*}.

Claim: E(A) underlies a canonical crystal in smooth groups E(A) on the nilpotent crystalline site, with E(A)_S ≅ E(A). The construction is functorial in A, compatible with base change, and the isomorphism is too. Concretely, E(A)_{S'} = E(A') for any abelian scheme A' lifting A to S'. One must give a transitive system of canonical isomorphisms between the results for different lifts.
- Characteristic 0: no divided powers are needed. A smooth group E' over a (nil-)thickening S' lifting E is unique up to unique isomorphism; the non-noetherian case follows by passing to the limit. This is the result of the 'old letter to Tate'.
- General case: one uses 'the method of the exponential', to be explained for Barsotti-Tate groups later.
- Alternative: E(A*) = R^1 f_{cris*}(G_m) on the absolute nilpotent crystalline topos of A. Crystalline G_m-torsors are line bundles with integrable (PD-)connection, so this is the crystalline Pic^♮.

The next page then identifies D*(A) = Lie E(A*). Fil^1 lifts correspond to lifts of the vector subgroup. Dividing by such a lift gives the dual of the deformed abelian scheme. This is the Mazur–Messing approach.
errors: The formula E(A*) = R^1 f_{cris*}(G_m) is stated loosely. R^1 f_{cris*}G_m gives the whole crystalline Picard (Pic^♮, line bundles with integrable connection), including Néron–Severi components. E(A*) should be its identity component (or the algebraically-equivalent-to-zero part). A rigidification along the zero section is also implicit.

Minor: the E in the char-0 sentence means E(A). The uniqueness 'à isomorphisme unique près' needs the universal extension's rigidity, i.e. that E(A) has no nontrivial infinitesimal automorphisms lifting identity. This holds because Hom(E(A), G_a) = 0, but the page does not argue it.

ideas.what: Universal vector extension E(A) of an abelian scheme carries a canonical crystal structure on the nilpotent crystalline site, E(A)_{S'} = E(A') for any lift A'
ideas.modern_name: crystalline nature of the universal vector extension
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (ICM Nice 1970); proofs by Mazur–Messing (LNM 370, 1974) and Messing (LNM 264, 1972)
ideas.where_published: Groupes de Barsotti-Tate et cristaux, Actes ICM Nice 1970; Montréal lectures 1970 (pub. 1974)

ideas.what: In characteristic 0 a smooth group lifting E(A) over a nil-thickening is unique up to unique isomorphism (letter to Tate)
ideas.modern_name: rigidity of the universal extension / crystalline nature in char 0
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (letter to Tate, 1966), used by Mazur–Messing
ideas.where_published: mentioned in ICM 1970 report; letter to Tate unpublished/circulated

ideas.what: Method of the exponential to build the crystal and prove the deformation theorem
ideas.modern_name: Grothendieck–Messing deformation theory via exponential on PD ideals

ideas.what: E(A*) = R^1 f_{cris*} G_m on the absolute nilpotent crystalline topos
ideas.modern_name: crystalline Picard / Pic^♮ as a crystal (line bundles with integrable connection)

deep.surprise_reason: Draft of material that appears essentially verbatim in Grothendieck's ICM 1970 report. It was fully developed by Messing and Mazur–Messing. Nothing here is absent from the literature.
transcription_corrections: In the extension 0 -> t_{A*} -> E(A) -> A -> 0 there is a handwritten check mark over t, with an overstruck *. It should read the dual tangent space of A* (i.e. ω_{A*}), consistent with the next page using t̆_A ⊂ D*(A)_S = Lie E(A*).
The 'E(A) ≃ E(A)_S' isomorphism symbol is overtyped; the intended reading is ≃.
The subscript in R^1 f_{Acris*} is overtyped ('Acris*'), with A_cris (topos) as the intended meaning.
